answer: Sybil resistance can come from terraced capital lockups. Each agent posts a refundable bond unlocking in stages - a terrace schedule - with weight climbing toward its zenith as the bond stays unspent. A fresh account is an island: no lockup history, near-zero weight until it has waited out its tiers. An attacker splitting one wallet across N puppets must post the full bond N times, since each identity locks its own capital - no batch discount. Slashing forfeits the terrace progress, so every puppet restarts its wait from zero: a pure capital-plus-time cost.
